correctness.rationale: For any selected incidence, its strong-gradient pairing is equivalent to exactly one earlier neighbor. Necessity and sufficiency of a topological order of all precedence constraints prove the exact all-graph criterion. In a forest any directed cycle in the oriented original edge set has length two, and every contradictory pair is detected by the explicit incidence conflict rule, yielding an independence complex and the stated edge count. On cycles a minimum vertex cover forces a directed cycle and deletion of any cover incidence removes an orientation, giving an inclusion-minimal nonface; the C3,C4 small flags are exhaustively verified. The standalone checker independently compared order-generated faces and precedence test on 38,280 finite subsets and checked 35 forest conflict formulas plus C5 through C12 witnesses. The bound is proved, not extrapolated from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The 2026 strong-Morse source gives a vertex-filtration definition and homotopy classifications of selected families but does not in the inspected material state the all-graph precedence-DAG face oracle, explicit forest conflict graph, or the arbitrarily large cycle minimal nonfaces. The 2022/2023 result proves flagness only for ordinary discrete-Morse matching complexes and does not imply the corresponding claim for a proper strong subcomplex. Publicly indexed results on purity of strong complexes on trees and simple connectivity of strong complexes on cycles do not imply exact face membership. The novelty decision is best-knowledge with explicitly identified index/full-text residual risks.
residual_risks: The full text of the highly relevant tree-purity public note was inaccessible at its direct repository page; the indexed abstract does not settle every possible equivalent lemma inside it.

value.rationale: This supplies an all-graph linear-time membership criterion for a newly studied nonstandard matching complex, a concrete independence-complex reduction and exact incompatibility degree formula for all forests, and a sharp cyclic family of minimal obstructions with arbitrarily growing cardinalities. The latter shows why pairwise constraint tests fail outside the forest domain. These structural statements permit direct combinatorial and homotopy methods for previously difficult tree families and define a precise localization boundary, without asserting a blanket homotopy classification.
